doc.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Army service in Alaska, Hawaii and Fort Lewis
summary: He played in Army bands, never went to Korea, and played cello to see off troop boats.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Were you sent overseas for the Korean War?

I went to Alaska and I went to Hawaii. I played “Rhapsody in Blue” in Hawaii. And up in Alaska we didn’t do very much of anything. But I was in Ft. Lewis, Seattle, mostly, playing for generals and captains, and that kind of stuff. No, I didn’t go to Korea but I played off a lot of guys. When I was in the war I used to play cello. And I would go, instead of playing cymbals, which is what they had me doing in the band, I would take

my cello out and we’d go to the boat and I’d have to be there so I’d take my cello and I’d play to guys. They’d look down and say, “Who’s playing the cello down there?” I played Pepper off — who else did I play off? I played a number of guys off. I was part of the band so we had to do it.
